**ACCEPT** — `domain:devx @ objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, R46, reviewed 2026-09-07T16:20Z against GitHub and the tree, ⛔ never against the report's narrative.

## What was verified independently

**The diff is what the report says it is.** `+151/-7` across exactly two files, draft, head `d7bd19901`. The resolver change is one added helper plus one call-site swap:

```js
const coveredPrefixes = [...coveredSet].map((member) => `${member}/`);
const isCovered = (spec) => coveredSet.has(spec) || coveredPrefixes.some((prefix) => spec.startsWith(prefix));
```

`holdsObtainedModule()` is absent from the diff (⇒ #8183's chain head is clean and #8183 rebases onto this), `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` gains no member (⇒ `@object-ui/app-shell` is not smuggled in ahead of #8173), and #8117 is not folded in. All three fences held.

**The load-bearing number was re-derived here, not taken from the report.** A `git grep` over `origin/main` for every `vi.mock('@object-ui/…')` specifier returns 22 distinct specifiers, of which **exactly one is a subpath — `@object-ui/components/ui/sonner`, at 2 call sites**, and `@object-ui/components` is a member of the 18-name constant. That is the report's population reproduced by a different instrument than the one it used (`scan()`), which is why it is being accepted rather than re-run.

## ⭐ The separator fence is not hypothetical — it has a live occupant, and this is the finding of the review

The PR and its pin justify including the `/` in the prefix with `@object-ui/react-native`, which does not exist. **A package that does exist is `@object-ui/react-runtime`** — enumerated from all 39 `@object-ui/*` workspace manifests on `origin/main` and checked against every member:

```
bare string-prefix collisions (member is a prefix of another package name): 1
  @object-ui/react  is a prefix of  @object-ui/react-runtime   swallowed by `member + '/'`? False
```

So a naive `spec.startsWith(member)` would have silently pulled a real, never-swept package into `covered` and judged it as though it had been — an over-claim in the *same* direction as the defect this card fixes, introduced by the fix. The implementation includes the separator, so it does not happen; the pin covers the shape (`${COVERED}-native`, `${COVERED}ive`). ⚠️ Recorded because the pin's example is invented while the hazard is real: if that pin is ever edited, `@object-ui/react-runtime` is the case that must keep passing.

## No stale consumer of the verdict string is left behind

The line changed from `… judged` to `… and their subpaths judged`. Searching `origin/main` for `call site(s) on` outside the gate returns **one** hit — `scripts/__tests__/check-vi-mock-inherit.test.ts:677` — and this PR updates it, in both the `summarise()` assertion and the real-spawn `toContain`. Control: the string does occur once in the gate itself, so the search was live rather than empty.

## The pins earn the claim

The regression pin builds a fixture with a frozen subpath factory and asserts `frozen === [subpath]`, `census.covered === 1`, `census.workspace === 0` — reverting the resolver reds it. The on-disk pin carries its own **existence control** (`${file} moved — this control tests nothing`), so it cannot pass vacuously if the two `plugin-form` files are renamed. And the structural pin — every member `.split('/')` has length 2 — is what keeps option 2 from being reintroduced by accident: it makes "the constant names package ROOTS only" a mechanically enforced sentence rather than a header claim.

⭐ The ablation the dev ran is the report's strongest line and it reproduces the card's thesis exactly: with the resolver reverted, **the pins go red while the gate itself still exits 0** printing `37 other workspace`. That is the card in one sentence — the gate cannot detect its own over-claim, so the pin is the only thing standing between this and a green that asserts more than it checked.

## Answering the dev's open question, because it has a measured answer

The dispatch's "⛔ no model identifiers in any pushed artifact" and this session's mandated `Co-Authored-By:` trailer do conflict on the letter. **Option A, as the dev chose — and the conflict is moot at the merge boundary:** this shift has measured three landings (`f20e57d62`, `dc75260a2`, `59cca05b0`) where the squash path normalises the trailer to a plain `Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` with no model identifier. Nothing carrying a model name reaches `main`. ⛔ Do not push a follow-up commit to rewrite it; that would add a commit to fix something the merge already fixes.

## Out-of-scope finding

#8392 (the `vi-mock-specifiers.yml` step comment now under-claiming) is correctly out of this PR's fenced surface and correctly filed rather than fixed. Verified on `origin/main`: `.github/workflows/vi-mock-specifiers.yml:113` does say what the card says it says. ⭐ The seat added the `finding` label the card was filed without — an observation card with no label is invisible to the grading sweep. ⛔ No `domain:*` and no grade were added: that is the triage seat's alone.

No changeset owed (`scripts/**` only; `check-changeset-presence` agrees).

Next: CI convergence → flip ready → post-flip guard → auto-merge SQUASH → queue confirmation → landing probe (`isCovered` and the `member + '/'` prefix present on re-fetched `origin/main`, the verdict line carrying `and their subpaths judged`; control: `@object-ui/react-runtime` still a package and still NOT a member) → LANDED here and on #8141, which closes via `Fixes`. **#8183 is dispatched only after this lands.**

LANDED — merged into `main` at 2026-09-07T16:40:49Z as `47053c9f6` (squash), read 16:41:01Z. #8141 closed `completed` via `Fixes`.

**Content probe on re-fetched `origin/main` (tip `47053c9f6`, read 2026-09-07T16:42Z)** — the two claims from the Armed note, plus the control:

1. **The resolver.** `scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs:1293-1294` carries `coveredPrefixes` built as `` `${member}/` `` and `isCovered = (spec) => coveredSet.has(spec) || coveredPrefixes.some(...)`, wired in at `:1311`. **The separator is present**, which is the whole safety of the change.
2. **The verdict line.** `:1426` reads `… and their subpaths judged`, so the sentence is now true of what the run checked.
3. **Control — and it is the one that matters, so it was re-run against the merged tree rather than assumed to still hold.** `@object-ui/react-runtime` is still a real workspace package (`packages/react-runtime/package.json`) and still **NOT** a `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` member (0 matches; the constant holds 18, unchanged by this PR). It is the single live bare string-prefix extension of a member (`@object-ui/react`) in the tree, so it is the case a lost separator would silently swallow. It is not swallowed.

⭐ Restating why that control is the right one: this PR's own hazard was introducing the defect it removes, one level up — a naive `startsWith(member)` would have pulled a never-swept package into `covered` and reported it as judged. The constant's count staying at 18 while the *reach* of each member widened is exactly the shape the header claims ("what widened is the reach of one membership, not the test for membership"), and both halves are now verifiable on main.

⇒ **#8183 is unblocked** — the chain head has landed, so it may be dispatched and will rebase onto this resolver rather than race it. #6892's `@object-ui/app-shell` slice is queued behind it on the same file.
